explanation.question_quote: a high-pitched, harsh, holosystolic murmur that is best heard at the lower left sternal border
explanation.sentence: The child has a harsh holosystolic murmur at the lower left sternal border and no cyanosis.
A holosystolic murmur at this location is characteristic of a ventricular septal defect.
In a left-to-right ventricular shunt, oxygenated blood flows from the higher-pressure left ventricle into the right ventricle, raising right ventricular oxygen tension above normal.
Because deoxygenated blood does not enter the left ventricle through the defect, left ventricular and systemic arterial oxygen tensions remain normal.
